entries.title: Evening Briefing · 26 November 2026
headlines: Houthis claim a strike on Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery; a projectile hits Jazan port
EU leaders split over a 1.58 trillion euro budget and a 45 billion euro Ukraine loan
India recalls Parliament from Monday 30 November, with a delimitation bill expected
FTSE 100 closes up 1.8% at 10,609.30
India A knocked out by Sri Lanka A; the NZ v India decider starts at 22:00 GMT

stories.headline: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia widen to ports and the Ras Tanura refinery
stories.summary: The Houthis say they hit Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, on Wednesday. The coalition says it downed four drones there and saw only falling debris. A projectile caused minor damage at Jazan port, a drone was stopped near Jeddah port, missiles at Riyadh were intercepted, and rebel-run media report new Saudi strikes on Sanaa.
stories.whyItMatters: Attacks on Gulf energy sites and Red Sea ports put oil and shipping at risk; Brent rose 3.5% on Wednesday.

stories.headline: Iran says tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iranian state media say two tankers struck mines and caught fire in a restricted zone of the strait on Wednesday. Nobody has confirmed this independently. Brent was down 0.87% at 93.79 dollars a barrel at 09:39 GMT after Wednesday's jump.
stories.whyItMatters: About a fifth of the world's oil normally passes through Hormuz, so any confirmed attack there would move energy prices.

stories.headline: EU summit deadlocked on the 2028-34 budget and a Ukraine loan
stories.summary: Leaders in Brussels are split over a 1.58 trillion euro seven-year budget and a 45 billion euro loan to Ukraine that would be repaid only if Russia pays reparations. Hungary, Slovakia, Czechia and Bulgaria object to the loan. Costa says talks could run into Friday, and a deal is now targeted for December.
stories.whyItMatters: Ukraine's funding for 2027 depends on the deal, and all 27 members must agree.

stories.headline: Explosion at Bangkok's Bangchak oil depot injures seven
stories.summary: A blast and fire hit the Bangchak facility in eastern Bangkok at about 14:45 local time, injuring seven people, four of them critically. The company says the fire was out within about half an hour, shut production units and is investigating the cause.
stories.whyItMatters: The site is one of Bangkok's main fuel plants, so investigators and the market will watch how long it stays offline.

stories.headline: Tube strike under way, the first of eight driver walkouts this winter
stories.summary: RMT drivers walked out at midday. The Circle and Piccadilly lines, including the Heathrow branch, did not run today, and service should be back to normal by about 18:00 on Friday. Seven more 24-hour strikes are set for 17 and 19 December, 4 and 6 January, and 17, 23 and 25 February.
stories.whyItMatters: The dispute over a voluntary four-day week for drivers is unresolved, so London faces repeated disruption into February.

stories.headline: Babcock wins an 8.7 billion pound MoD submarine support contract
stories.summary: The Ministry of Defence awarded Babcock a five-year deal worth about 8.7 billion pounds to maintain and support Royal Navy submarines. Its shares rose 6.6%.
stories.whyItMatters: It secures work at the UK's submarine bases as defence spending rises.

stories.headline: Government recalls Parliament for 30 November to 3 December
stories.summary: Kiren Rijiju said the Lok Sabha will sit from Monday 30 November and the Rajya Sabha from 2 December, for essential government business, without naming bills. Congress says the aim is a delimitation bill that would raise Lok Sabha seats to 850, which failed in April, and calls it an attack on the Constitution. Opposition strategists meet on Friday at 16:30 IST.
stories.whyItMatters: Delimitation would redraw how seats are shared between states and is tied to women's reservation, and passing it needs a two-thirds majority.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules or fee changes today
stories.summary: The Home Office's GOV.UK page shows no visa, settlement, fee or citizenship announcements on 24 to 26 November, and no new Statement of Changes. The latest items are from 18 to 19 November: the Immigration and Asylum Bill passed the Commons and went to the Lords, and Professor Jackline Wahba became chair of the Migration Advisory Committee.
stories.whyItMatters: Earned settlement is confirmed but has no in-force date yet. The rules are due to start being laid from the December Immigration Rules and phased in during 2027, so Indian Skilled Workers should watch the December Statement of Changes.

stories.headline: Sri Lanka A knock India A out of the Rising Stars Asia Cup
stories.summary: India A made 317 for 8 in Doha, with 78 from Abhishek Sharma. Sri Lanka A won by eight wickets with 51 balls left, led by centuries from Lasith Croospulle (116) and Sineth Jayawardena (105). Sri Lanka A play the final on Sunday 29 November.
stories.whyItMatters: It is an early exit for a strong India A squad that included several senior internationals.

stories.headline: NZ v India second Test starts tonight at 22:00 GMT
stories.summary: The toss at Hagley Oval, Christchurch, is at 21:30 GMT. The series is 0-0 after the draw in Wellington, so India must win to level it. NZ seamer Blair Tickner is out injured and Matt Fisher has been called up.
stories.whyItMatters: India are fourth in the World Test Championship and need wins to stay in the race for the final.

stories.headline: FCC approves SpaceX's plan for a million data-centre satellites
stories.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission authorised SpaceX's Starmind constellation of up to one million satellites for computing in orbit. The first satellites must launch by November 2033 and the full system must be running by 2040. There was no major ISRO or NASA mission news today.
stories.whyItMatters: A system that size would dwarf every satellite now in orbit and adds to concerns about space debris and astronomy.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 closes up 1.8% at 10,609.30 on bid talk, miners and defence
stories.summary: Thursday close: FTSE 100 10,609.30, up 182.36 points (1.75%). Imperial Brands rose about 13% after Altria said it is considering a possible cash offer, miners rallied on higher metal prices, and Babcock added 6.6%. The FTSE 250 rose 1.9%.
stories.whyItMatters: London recovered Wednesday's tariff and inflation losses, with thin volumes because US markets were shut.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty end a choppy day higher, led by IT and realty
stories.summary: Thursday close: Sensex 84,328.59, up 390.31 points (0.46%), and Nifty 50 25,884.50, up 65.25 (0.25%), a third straight gain. Indices gave up early gains on oil worries before IT stocks such as TCS and HCL Tech and property shares led a recovery.
stories.whyItMatters: Foreign buying is holding up Indian stocks despite the US tariff threat and higher oil prices.

stories.headline: Wall Street closed for Thanksgiving; Wednesday's late rebound still stands
stories.summary: US exchanges are closed today. Wednesday 25 November close: Dow 50,182.95 (up 0.33%), S&P 500 7,182.78 (down 0.25%), Nasdaq Composite 23,585.80 (down 0.62%), after a sharp early drop on inflation data and the US tariff plan.
stories.whyItMatters: Friday's short session and any oil moves from the Gulf will set the tone for next week.

entries.title: Morning Briefing · 26 November 2026
headlines: Houthi missiles fired at Riyadh are intercepted; blast hits Sanaa as Brent jumps 3.5%
Wall Street recovers from a deep intraday slump; US markets shut today for Thanksgiving
India rejects the US excess capacity finding behind a 25% tariff threat
London Tube strike from midday today, with no Tube service after 9pm
Liverpool win 3-0 in Bruges; Manchester United draw 2-2 at Sporting

stories.headline: Houthi missiles at Riyadh intercepted as strikes hit Sanaa
stories.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh overnight, while an explosion shook Sanaa after air strikes near its airport. UKMTO logged a tanker reporting a blast from an unknown projectile about 50 nautical miles west of Dubai, with no injuries or damage. Houthi claims of hits on Ras Tanura and the Jeddah and Jizan ports remain unconfirmed.
stories.whyItMatters: The Yemen front is now reaching Saudi cities and Gulf shipping lanes. Brent settled 3.5% higher at 94.61 dollars on Wednesday.

stories.headline: Fuel tanker fire on a Cairo ring road kills at least 31
stories.summary: A fuel tanker overturned and caught fire on a major highway around Cairo on Wednesday evening, setting vehicles alight. Egypt's health ministry put the toll at at least 31 dead and 21 injured.
stories.whyItMatters: The toll may rise: officials say several survivors have burns over most of their bodies.

stories.headline: RMT Tube strike runs from midday today to midday Friday
stories.summary: London Underground workers in the RMT walk out from 12:00 today until 11:59 on Friday over new working arrangements after talks failed. TfL says the Piccadilly and Circle lines will not run today, all lines are disrupted from noon and the network shuts after 21:00, with normal service by about 18:00 Friday. The Overground runs as usual.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the first of eight strike dates announced, with more set for December, January and February.

stories.headline: BBC journalists vote for strike action over 500 million pound cuts
stories.summary: NUJ members at the BBC backed strikes by 79.4% on a 75% turnout, and 91.3% backed action short of a strike, over cuts, forced redundancies and workloads. The mandate lasts 12 months and no dates have been set.
stories.whyItMatters: Walkouts could disrupt BBC news programmes while the corporation pushes through deep savings.

stories.headline: India rejects US claim of structural excess capacity
stories.summary: After the US Trade Representative named India among 16 economies it says add to global overcapacity and proposed tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, or 17% with a trade deal, the Commerce Ministry said India has no structural excess capacity in any sector. It said trade concerns should be handled in the bilateral trade agreement talks.
stories.whyItMatters: The tariffs are only proposed, but they put a clock on the India-US trade deal.

stories.headline: Supreme Court sets aside order for CBI and ED checks on Rahul Gandhi
stories.summary: A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant quashed an Allahabad High Court order that had told the CBI and ED to verify disproportionate-assets allegations against Rahul Gandhi. The case returns to a fresh High Court bench, which must hear him and first decide whether the petition is maintainable.
stories.whyItMatters: It removes an immediate investigative threat to Gandhi, though the allegations themselves were not ruled on.

stories.headline: Constitution Day turns political; 26/11 victims remembered
stories.summary: India marks the 77th Constitution Day today, also the anniversary of the 2008 Mumbai attacks. PM Modi used an op-ed to attack Congress over the Emergency, while Congress holds Samvidhan Raksha marches in several states over alleged voter-roll deletions.
stories.whyItMatters: Voter-roll accuracy is becoming the opposition's main theme for the 2027 state polls.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules or Home Office immigration announcements
stories.summary: GOV.UK's Home Office news through 25 November shows nothing on visas, settlement, fees or citizenship, and no new Statement of Changes has been reported this week. Earned settlement remains confirmed policy with no start date because its rules have not been laid. It makes 10 years the default route to ILR, 5 years for those earning over 50,271 pounds, with B2 English required.
stories.whyItMatters: Skilled Worker visa holders, including many Indian nationals, should keep applying under the current rules until the new rules are laid and dated.

stories.headline: Liverpool beat Club Brugge 3-0 in the Champions League
stories.summary: Alexander Isak scored early and late and Florian Wirtz curled in a third at the Jan Breydel Stadium. Liverpool have 12 points from five league-phase games and host Porto next.
stories.whyItMatters: It keeps Liverpool in the top eight, the places that skip the knockout play-off round.

stories.headline: Manchester United draw 2-2 at Sporting; Bayern lose to Lille
stories.summary: United were held in Lisbon and had a late Sporting own goal ruled out for a foul. PSG drew with Roma, Lille beat Bayern Munich and Inter won at Stuttgart.
stories.whyItMatters: United's draw leaves their place in the top eight in doubt with three league-phase games left.

stories.headline: Cricket today: India A semi-final at 10:00, Christchurch Test at 22:00 GMT
stories.summary: India A play unbeaten Sri Lanka A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars semi-final in Doha from 10:00 GMT, with the final on Sunday. At 22:00 GMT New Zealand and India start the second and final Test at Hagley Oval with the series level.
stories.whyItMatters: India need to win in Christchurch to take the series.

stories.headline: Europa League tonight: Bournemouth, Palace, Sunderland and Celtic
stories.summary: Bournemouth visit Celta Vigo at 17:45 UK time. At 20:00 Crystal Palace host Real Sociedad, Sunderland host Jagiellonia and Celtic visit Torreense.
stories.whyItMatters: Matchday 5 of 8 is where top-eight places in the league phase start to settle.

stories.headline: Quiet night for space; Cygnus NG-25 still due on Sunday
stories.summary: No major ISRO, NASA or other mission news broke overnight. Northrop Grumman's NG-25 cargo flight to the ISS remains listed for a Falcon 9 launch from Cape Canaveral on Sunday 29 November.

stories.headline: Wall Street claws back an AI and inflation sell-off; FTSE slipped 0.38%
stories.summary: Wednesday close: Dow 50,182.95 (+0.33%), S&P 500 7,182.78 (-0.25%), Nasdaq Composite 23,585.80 (-0.62%), after the S&P had been down as much as 3.2% on hot PCE inflation, the US tariff plan and AI-stock selling. The FTSE 100 closed at 10,426.94, down 0.38%. US markets are closed today for Thanksgiving and close early on Friday.
stories.whyItMatters: Markets now treat a December Fed rate rise as likely, keeping pressure on borrowing costs worldwide.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty extend Wednesday's rally on IT buying, still trading
stories.summary: Live at 09:20 IST: Sensex 84,326.40 (+388.12, +0.46%) and Nifty 50 25,880.00 (+60.75, +0.23%), led by IT stocks. Foreign investors have bought for 11 sessions in a row, about 14 billion dollars this month.
stories.whyItMatters: Foreign buying is shielding Indian stocks from the US tariff threat, though Brent above 95 dollars and a weak rupee are risks.

stories.headline: Asian stocks rebound; Bank of Korea reported to raise rates
stories.summary: In Thursday's session the Nikkei 225 was up about 1.2%, the Kospi about 1.7% and the Hang Seng about 1.5%. One report says the Bank of Korea raised its base rate by a quarter point to 3.25%; this is not yet confirmed by the central bank.
stories.whyItMatters: A rate rise in Korea would show inflation pressure spreading beyond the US.

entries.title: Evening Briefing · 25 November 2026
headlines: Wall Street claws back from an AI rout after hot inflation data; the Dow turns positive and the Nasdaq trims a 4% fall to about 1%
US proposes new tariffs on 14 economies, with up to 25% on India
Saudi-led coalition confirms strikes on Yemen's Hodeidah port as the Houthis threaten Jeddah
Supreme Court refuses Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam interim bail for now and sends the case towards a three-judge bench
Indian shares close up about 1.8% while the FTSE 100 slips 0.38%

stories.headline: Coalition confirms Hodeidah strikes; Houthis threaten Saudi Red Sea ports
stories.summary: The Saudi-led coalition confirmed it struck military capabilities at Yemen's Hodeidah port and targets in Saada and Amran late on Tuesday, after warning civilians to leave. The Houthis told workers and shipping firms to leave Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports. The coalition said it downed four drones over Ras Tanura with no casualties; Houthi claims of refinery fires are unconfirmed.
stories.whyItMatters: Hodeidah handles most of Yemen's aid imports, and a threat to Jeddah would carry the war onto the Red Sea shipping lane.

stories.headline: US proposes tariffs on 14 trading partners, up to 25% for India
stories.summary: The US Trade Representative proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies over excess industrial capacity, with reported rates of about 20% more on China, 15% for the EU and Japan, and up to 25% for India, or 17% with a trade deal. Comments are due by 5 January 2027 and hearings start on 25 January.
stories.whyItMatters: India's rate is among the highest on the list, raising pressure on trade talks with Washington. The plan helped drive the early market sell-off.

stories.headline: Russia launches 112 drones at Ukraine; refinery hits still unconfirmed
stories.summary: Ukraine's air force said it downed 88 of 112 drones overnight, with hits in 18 places and deaths in the Kyiv, Kharkiv and Chernihiv regions. The injury toll from Tuesday's Zaporizhzhia strike rose to 50. Fires were reported at the Syzran and Novokuibyshevsk refineries, but there is no official confirmation the plants were hit.
stories.whyItMatters: Putin said on Tuesday that retaliation for refinery strikes is inevitable, and Trump said he is under no deadline for a peace deal.

stories.headline: Solomon Islands signs treaty with Australia barring foreign bases
stories.summary: The Solomon Islands and Australia signed a treaty ruling out any foreign military base in the Solomons. Honiara said it will not renew its 2022 security pact with China.
stories.whyItMatters: It reverses one of Beijing's biggest security gains in the Pacific.

stories.headline: PMQs: Badenoch presses Burnham on EU student fees
stories.summary: Kemi Badenoch asked whether last week's EU reset deal will let EU students pay home fees, capped at 9,790 pounds, instead of international rates. Andy Burnham said the fees deal is not done and the issue has not been put on the table.
stories.whyItMatters: Universities say home-fee status for EU students could cost them hundreds of millions of pounds a year.

stories.headline: Independent panel to examine nuclear test veterans' treatment
stories.summary: The Prime Minister set up an independent panel chaired by Bishop James Jones, who led the Hillsborough panel, to look at how Cold War nuclear tests affected veterans and their descendants and at claims of a cover-up. An interim report is due before 3 October 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: Veterans have campaigned for decades, and oversight moves from the Ministry of Defence to the Cabinet Office.

stories.headline: Supreme Court refuses Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam interim bail for now
stories.summary: A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant refused interim bail for now in the 2020 Delhi riots UAPA case. It issued notice to Delhi Police and asked the Registry to put the case before the Chief Justice to set up a three-judge bench. No next date was given.
stories.whyItMatters: Both men have been jailed since 2020 without trial witnesses being examined, and a larger bench may settle how long UAPA accused can be held before trial.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves 2,014 crore rupee airport at Doloo in Assam
stories.summary: The Union Cabinet cleared a new greenfield airport at Doloo, the second for Assam's Barak Valley, built for about 10.1 lakh passengers a year.
stories.whyItMatters: It adds air capacity in a poorly connected part of the northeast.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules or Home Office announcements today
stories.summary: Nothing new on GOV.UK since this morning. Earned settlement is confirmed policy, announced on 2 November with a full consultation response on 12 November, but its Immigration Rules have not been laid and no start date is set. The plan makes 10 years the default route to settlement, 5 years for those earning over 50,271 pounds, and requires B2 English.
stories.whyItMatters: Skilled Worker visa holders planning for ILR should watch for the Statement of Changes expected in December. Student maintenance funds rise on 30 November 2026.

stories.headline: Christchurch Test starts at 10pm UK time on Thursday
stories.summary: The second and final Test between New Zealand and India starts at 11am local on Friday at Hagley Oval, which is 22:00 GMT on Thursday. The series is level after the Wellington draw, and New Zealand are without Mitchell Santner, with Dean Foxcroft called up.
stories.whyItMatters: India need a win to keep their World Test Championship final hopes on track.

stories.headline: Champions League tonight: Liverpool without Gakpo in Bruges
stories.summary: Liverpool visit Club Brugge and Manchester United play Sporting in Lisbon, both at 8pm UK time, with Cody Gakpo out injured for Liverpool. Roma visit PSG, Bayern play Lille and Stuttgart face Inter.
stories.whyItMatters: United are 17th in the league phase and need points to avoid the play-off places.

stories.headline: ISRO chief says Gaganyaan is not delayed but gives no date
stories.summary: V Narayanan said on Tuesday that the uncrewed G1 flight is in its final phase, with the rocket ready and the orbital module still being worked on, and will fly at the earliest opportunity. He was responding to reports that G1 might slip to February 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: G1 must fly before India can attempt its first crewed spaceflight.

stories.headline: Cygnus NG-25 cargo flight to the ISS lined up for 29 November
stories.summary: Launch schedules list Northrop Grumman's NG-25 resupply mission on a Falcon 9 from Cape Canaveral on Sunday, alongside a US Space Force launch from Vandenberg the same day.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the next cargo run to the space station.

stories.headline: Wall Street recovers most of a steep AI sell-off, still trading
stories.summary: Live at 13:37 ET (18:37 GMT): Dow 50,217.17 (+0.40%), S&P 500 7,163.29 (-0.52%), Nasdaq Composite 23,451.46 (-1.19%). October PCE inflation of 3.8%, core 3.3% against 3.2% expected, and the tariff plan sent the Nasdaq down over 4% and the Dow down more than 1,000 points early on, with the Nasdaq-100 briefly in bear-market territory. Markets now price a December Fed hike as almost certain.
stories.whyItMatters: A Nasdaq-100 close below 24,979.58 would confirm a bear market. US markets are shut on Thursday for Thanksgiving and the Fed meets on 8 and 9 December.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 closes 0.38% lower as tech names follow the US
stories.summary: Wednesday close: FTSE 100 10,426.94 (-40.13, -0.38%), FTSE 250 down 0.9%. Computacenter fell 8.2% and Autotrader 3.3% after Amazon said Amazon Autos will launch in the UK in early 2027, while Imperial Brands rose 6.1% and Unilever 2.2%.
stories.whyItMatters: US inflation and tariff worries reached London despite its small tech weighting.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty close up about 1.8% after the holiday
stories.summary: Wednesday close: Sensex 83,938.28 (+1,502.29, +1.82%) and Nifty 50 25,819.25 (+469.60, +1.85%), slightly below the midday highs. FMCG led, with Hindustan Unilever up about 6%, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank rose over 3%, and Tata Steel fell 2.3%.
stories.whyItMatters: Foreign buying and lower crude lifted the rupee to an eight-month high.

entries.title: Morning Briefing · 25 November 2026
headlines: The Gulf conflict widens to Saudi Arabia as Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition trade strikes
Chip selloff hits Asia: Kospi down 5.6% and Nikkei 3.6% after the Nasdaq fell 1.5%, while the Dow closed back above 50,000
Indian shares jump over 2% after the holiday, with the Sensex up about 1,900 points at midday
Shenzhou-24 docks with China's space station carrying the first foreign astronaut on Tiangong
The Akali Dal rejoins the NDA for Punjab's 2027 election

stories.headline: Houthis and Saudi Arabia trade strikes as the Gulf war widens
stories.summary: A Houthi strike on a tower in Riyadh's financial district injured 11 people on Tuesday. The Houthis say Saudi forces struck Hodeidah port overnight, a claim not yet independently confirmed, and the Saudi-led coalition says it downed four drones over the Ras Tanura oil terminal. Israel's defence minister separately accused Iran of developing chemical weapons, which Tehran denies.
stories.whyItMatters: A Saudi front, with oil sites now targeted, adds a second risk to energy supplies alongside the Hormuz blockade.

stories.headline: Huawei convicted on 10 of 12 counts in its US fraud trial
stories.summary: A federal jury in Brooklyn found Huawei guilty of bank fraud, Iran-related sanctions breaches and conspiring to steal trade secrets. It was cleared of racketeering conspiracy and obstruction. Sentencing is set for September 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: The verdict adds to US-China tech friction just days after the Trump, Xi and Putin summit.

stories.headline: Trump says a pardon for Nvidia's Jensen Huang is always an option
stories.summary: Trump told the New York Post a pardon was possible but probably not needed, a day after Huang was reinstated as Nvidia chief executive. The Attorney General would not say whether Huang is under federal investigation. Huang is due before House and Senate committees next week.
stories.whyItMatters: It ties the White House to the world's most valuable chipmaker while that company faces a national-security inquiry, and Nvidia's swings are driving global markets.

stories.headline: Ukrainian drones reportedly hit two Russian refineries overnight
stories.summary: Reports citing the Institute for the Study of War say drones struck the Syzran and Kuibyshev refineries in Samara region, starting fires. Neither Reuters nor AP had confirmed it at the time of writing. On Tuesday Putin said retaliation for refinery attacks was inevitable.
stories.whyItMatters: Refinery strikes cut Russia's fuel income, and Putin has threatened to escalate in response.

stories.headline: PMQs at noon, then a Conservative Opposition Day
stories.summary: Andy Burnham faces Kemi Badenoch at Prime Minister's Questions after Northern Ireland questions at 11:30. A Tory-led Opposition Day debate follows, on a subject not yet announced. The Lords continue the Health Bill in committee.
stories.whyItMatters: Capita's pension failures, the EU deal and welfare costs are likely flashpoints, weeks before the PM's 10-year plan is due.

stories.headline: Capita's chief executive quits over Civil Service pension failures
stories.summary: Adolfo Hernandez stepped down with immediate effect over problems running the Civil Service Pension Scheme, which has about 1.7 million members. Capita plans a 190 million pound share raise and expects a 95 million pound hit to 2027 profits. Its shares fell sharply to their lowest level in decades.
stories.whyItMatters: Unions want the contract brought in-house, which puts the government's use of outsourcers under pressure.

stories.headline: Cold snap squeezes the power grid
stories.summary: The grid operator NESO issued an Electricity Margin Notice for Tuesday afternoon and evening, as spare capacity fell below its preferred buffer. Wholesale power prices rose above 260 pounds per MWh, and NESO asked large industrial users to cut demand. It stressed that blackouts were not expected.
stories.whyItMatters: It is an early test of winter energy security and of costs that feed into household bills.

stories.headline: Private-sector growth slows in November
stories.summary: The flash composite PMI fell to 52.3 from 52.9, still showing growth for a fifth month. Manufacturing grew at its fastest pace since August 2024, but services slowed and firms cut jobs.
stories.whyItMatters: Weaker hiring feeds the Bank of England's rate debate as the Finance Bill moves through the Commons.

stories.headline: The Akali Dal returns to the NDA for Punjab 2027
stories.summary: The BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal announced their reunion in Delhi on Guru Nanak's Parkash Purab. Amit Shah called the SAD the BJP's oldest ally, and Modi called it a natural alliance. No seat-sharing terms were given.
stories.whyItMatters: The SAD quit the NDA in 2020 over the farm laws, so the deal reshapes the contest against AAP in Punjab.

stories.headline: Sibal warns the opposition against a delimitation seat hike offer
stories.summary: Kapil Sibal said the government is offering every state 50 percent more Lok Sabha seats to win support for a delimitation and women's reservation amendment. He also said leaving the Monsoon Session open without calling a Winter Session was unconstitutional, as it allows a sitting at two days' notice.
stories.whyItMatters: The amendment failed in April; a sudden new push would reopen the North-South row over representation.

stories.headline: Supreme Court hears Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam's new bail pleas today
stories.summary: A bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant takes up their challenge to the Delhi High Court's September refusal of bail in the 2020 Delhi riots UAPA case. They argue the trial is too slow and witness evidence will not finish before January.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a closely watched test of long detention before trial under the anti-terror law.

stories.headline: Modi and Merz review the India-Germany partnership
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz phoned Modi on Tuesday to review defence and technology ties and mark 75 years of diplomatic relations. Both said the India-EU trade deal would open new trade and investment.
stories.whyItMatters: It signals momentum on the EU deal, though no specific agreements were announced.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules or Home Office announcements since Monday
stories.summary: GOV.UK shows only routine updates, and earned settlement remains confirmed policy whose rules have not yet been laid; the first are expected in a December Statement of Changes. Dates to note: student maintenance funds rise on 30 November 2026, B2 English for settlement on specified routes from 26 March 2027, and Skilled Worker occupation thresholds move to the 25th percentile in spring 2027.
stories.whyItMatters: Most Skilled Workers earning under about 50,000 pounds face a 10-year path to ILR once the new rules start, so watch for the December statement and its transitional terms.

stories.headline: Champions League: Villa lose in Istanbul, Arsenal and City held
stories.summary: Galatasaray beat Aston Villa 1-0 with a late goal from substitute Deniz Gul. Arsenal drew 1-1 with Dortmund despite 30 shots, and Man City came back to draw 2-2 with Napoli through a late Cherki goal. Real Madrid thrashed PSV 5-1.
stories.whyItMatters: All three English sides dropped points, leaving Arsenal 5th, City 6th and Villa 7th with three games left.

stories.headline: Tonight: Liverpool at Club Brugge, Man Utd at Sporting
stories.summary: Both games kick off at 8pm UK time. Pochettino's United sit 17th in the league phase, with Cunha suspended and Sesko, Ugarte and Baleba injured.
stories.whyItMatters: United need points to stay in the top 24 and reach the knockout play-offs.

stories.headline: Sport's top court hands the 2025 AFCON title back to Senegal
stories.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport overturned the African confederation's March ruling that had awarded Morocco a 3-0 win. Senegal's 1-0 victory in the January final stands.
stories.whyItMatters: It ends a long and bitter dispute over who won Africa's biggest tournament.

stories.headline: India A face Sri Lanka A in Thursday's semi-final
stories.summary: The Rising Stars Asia Cup semi-final is at West End Park, Doha, at 10:00 GMT (3:30pm IST), with Tilak Varma captaining India A. Bangladesh A play Pakistan A on Friday, and the final is on 29 November.
stories.whyItMatters: India A arrive in form after Sooryavanshi's 204 off 53 balls in the group stage.

stories.headline: India need a win in Christchurch from Friday
stories.summary: The second and final Test against New Zealand starts at Hagley Oval on Friday, with the series level after a high-scoring draw in Wellington. Shubman Gill has signalled few changes to his side.
stories.whyItMatters: A draw would hurt India's World Test Championship hopes.

stories.headline: Shenzhou-24 docks with Tiangong carrying the first foreign astronaut
stories.summary: A Long March 2F lifted off from Jiuquan at 00:18 GMT, and the capsule docked with the Tianhe core module about 3.5 hours later. The crew are Tang Hongbo, Wu Yi and Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali.
stories.whyItMatters: It is China's first crewed mission with another country, a step in using its station for diplomacy.

stories.headline: Wall Street splits: Dow back above 50,000, Nasdaq down 1.5%
stories.summary: Tuesday close: Dow 50,018.70 (+0.85%), S&P 500 7,201.09 (-0.50%), Nasdaq Composite 23,733.54 (-1.48%). Chipmakers gave back part of Monday's rally, with Nvidia down almost 6% and the Philadelphia chip index about 8%, while money moved into healthcare and value stocks.
stories.whyItMatters: Traders now price a December Fed rate rise as near-certain, which weighs on richly valued tech.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 edges down as miners slide
stories.summary: Tuesday close: FTSE 100 10,467.07 (-0.13%). Antofagasta, Anglo American and Glencore fell 5% to 8% on weaker metals, while Experian, Compass and Relx rose. Pets at Home reports half-year results today.
stories.whyItMatters: Asia's chip rout points to a soft open in London this morning.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty rally over 2% as India reopens, still trading
stories.summary: At 12:00 IST (06:30 GMT) the Sensex was up 1,916 points (+2.32%) at 84,352.46 and the Nifty 50 up 567 points (+2.24%) at 25,916.90, after Tuesday's Guru Nanak Jayanti holiday. HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Bajaj Finance and Infosys led the gains.
stories.whyItMatters: India is catching up on the global rally it missed and recovering Monday's 1.8% fall, helped by foreign buying.

stories.headline: Asian chip stocks tumble: Kospi down 5.6%, Nikkei down 3.6%
stories.summary: By about 04:05 GMT the Kospi was down 5.6% and the Nikkei down 3.6%, with Taiwan's market off more than 6%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose 1%, and Brent crude slipped to about 88 dollars.
stories.whyItMatters: Asia reversed Monday's surge, a sign of how fragile the AI trade remains.
